html:
Dubai is the largest city of the United Arab Emirates, on a creek on the Persian Gulf coast. It is the capital of the emirate of the same name, ruled by the Al Maktoum family.

It began in the early 1700s as a small fishing and pearling village. The Al Maktoum took charge in 1833, and later in the 1800s the sheikhs signed truces with Britain, which made the coast the Trucial States under British protection. In 1901 Dubai made itself a free port, and merchants from Persia and India settled there. The pearl trade collapsed in the 1930s with cultured pearls and the Great Depression.

Oil was found in 1966, but much less than in neighbouring Abu Dhabi. Dubai joined the new UAE in 1971, and its rulers used the money to turn the city into a hub:

  • The deep-water Jebel Ali Port and its free zone, from the late 1970s.
  • The airline Emirates, founded in 1985, and one of the world's busiest airports.
  • Finance, property and tourism, with landmarks such as the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building since 2010.

Around nine in ten of its people are foreigners, many of them workers from South Asia who built the city, often under harsh conditions. Its model of glittering growth was copied around the Gulf, as by Qatar for the 2022 World Cup.
sum: Dubai is the largest city of the United Arab Emirates, on a creek on the Persian Gulf coast. It is the capital of the emirate of the same name, ruled by the Al Maktoum family.
